main_text.p: uah,ad me,quiescestes: & si abstuleris abominationes tuas à facie mea, non demigrabis. cap.4.1.

Sed hæc de orationis forma quæritur. An ne dubitantis oratio fit: Quis scit si conuertatur, &c. an uero affirmatis, bene de misericordia Dei & de uenia Niniuitis †sperandum? Respondeo: Cùm studio uerae resipiscentiae nulla res magis aduerse-tur, quàm dubitatio de misericordia Dei, & de uenia & mitigatione malorum: non est consentaneum, Regem, qui unicè uellet & optaret suos ciues una secum resipiscere, hoc orationis schemate dubios de salutari fructu conuersionis relinquere uoluisse. Immò contrà, ut τὰ [?], sic τὰ ἐλπιζόμενα certa uideri & haberi uolebat. Aduersatur igitur consilio Regis, dubitationis illud commentum.

[?]Etsi autem non semper distinguitur remissio pœnæ temporalis à remissione culpæ: ut ostendunt exempla, Dauidis, qui homicidij & adulterij graues dedit pœ-nas: Mosis, qui, quòd ad petram diffiden-tia peccasset, non potuit impetrare copi-am introeundi terram Patribus promis-sam: sæpe tamen Deus etiam temporales poenas

page.notes: Marginal marks: a dagger beside "sperandum" and a small sign (not clearly legible) beside "Etsi"; the second sign is doubtful. The first Greek word is smudged and only partly legible; the first letters appear to be τὰ followed by a word resembling πράγματα. The printed "cap.4.1." at the end of the first line is part of the text line, not a separate note. The printed "Niniuitis" and the "poenas" catchword are as they appear on the scan. Hyphens were kept where they stand at line ends.
